sources.provider: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer; layer BuildingShapesZip4 (service publisher not stated in the layer response)
sources.source_date: not supplied in the service record
sources.measurement_method: Used the feature's single outer ring. Converted EPSG:3857 vertices to WGS84 with spherical Web Mercator inverse formulas, then to the project's approximate local campus XY formula from modular/AGENTS.md. Plan area was computed from the converted project XY polygon; the source Shape__Area is Web Mercator area and is not treated as ground area.
sources.uncertainty: The feature name and street address strongly identify Hillel, but the layer's publisher/source date and survey status are not identified. NUM_LEVELS and 12 ft Extrution are GIS attributes, not architectural measured elevations. The feature may describe the pre-addition footprint; see the separate 2019 record below.

sources.role: parcel / aerial alignment and site context
sources.provider: Tippecanoe County Area Plan Commission agenda center; drawing by TBird Design Services Corp.
sources.source_crs: Survey monument table lists northing/easting/elevation but drawing does not state a CRS; not used for numeric model georeferencing.
sources.measurement_method: Reviewed the 1 in = 20 ft sketch plan and its 2019 aerial underlay. Used the Hillel parcel label, street layout, and visible existing roof to check the GIS footprint's address and corner-site context. The report says the existing building crossed an old platted lot line and that expansion was planned; the plan is a subdivision sketch and proposed-use document, not an as-built architectural plan.
sources.uncertainty: Aerial-underlay registration and roof-edge visibility are limited by overprinted survey annotations. The proposed addition is not assumed to have been built. The drawing gives no elevations or roof pitch.

sources.role: building identity, approximate floor area, front orientation and historic use
sources.provider: Tippecanoe County Area Board of Zoning Appeals
reported_facts: The existing Purdue Hillel Jewish Center is at 912 W. State Street.
The representative described the building as built in 1951 and roughly 6,500 sq ft.
An 845 sq ft addition was proposed in 2019; the minutes discuss that addition as a proposal.
The hearing record says the building front faces Waldron Street.
sources.measurement_method: Used the approximate reported building area only as an independent check against the converted GIS polygon area. Used the written front-orientation statement to orient the schematic entrance to the west/Waldron side.
sources.uncertainty: The stated area is approximate and the minutes are not a measured as-built drawing. No completed-construction record for the proposed 845 sq ft addition was found during this pass.

sources.role: current public address and Hillel organization cross-check
reported_facts: Purdue Hillel lists 912 Mitch Daniels Boulevard, West Lafayette.
sources.measurement_method: Cross-checked the current address against the former State Street address in the County plan and GIS feature. State Street was renamed Mitch Daniels Boulevard; the source check establishes organization/site continuity, not geometry.
sources.uncertainty: No building dimensions or architectural details are supplied by this page.

sources.role: direct exterior facade and roof-form reference; building continuity check
sources.provider: Purdue Hillel Foundation, official Spring 2022 newsletter
sources.source_crs: not applicable; photograph is not georeferenced
sources.measurement_method: Visual inspection of the exterior photograph on newsletter page 1. The photo directly supports a low single-storey composition, light buff masonry, repeated tall multi-pane window bays, a broad shallow flat/low-slope roof edge, and a distinct masonry/signage panel. No dimensions were extracted.
sources.uncertainty: Camera view is not compass-georeferenced and no elevations or dimensions are provided. The modeled broad eave, window locations/sizes, entry position, and wall height remain approximations. Newsletter text describes the 70-year-old building at 912 West State Street and remarks that it looks the same, but this is not proof about the 2019 proposed addition.

geometry_decisions.footprint: Use feature 803 ring unchanged after the documented coordinate conversion. Its 610.947 m2 project-plane area is close to the approximately 6,500 sq ft (603.87 m2) hearing figure, supporting identity and footprint scale.
geometry_decisions.height: Retain a 3.6576 m display placeholder for visual continuity only. It is numerically the former GIS Extrution=12 interpreted as feet, but the field units are undocumented; no measured height or 12 ft claim is made. Height remains unverified.
geometry_decisions.roof: A broad, flat/low-slope roof edge and pale roof finish are modeled from the Spring 2022 official newsletter photograph. The 0.7 m approximate overhang is visual only; no pitch or dimension is measured.
geometry_decisions.facade: Revised to light buff masonry, repeated tall framed multi-pane glazing, a distinct entry door and sign-panel mass, and broad eaves, guided by the official Spring 2022 exterior photograph. County minutes establish the west/Waldron-facing front; the photograph itself is not compass-registered. Opening sizes and positions remain illustrative.
geometry_decisions.placement: Keep the source's campus-world coordinate frame and stable scene/collection. Do not change the master placement marker or manifest.
geometry_decisions.2019_addition: Preserve the pre-addition feature 803 footprint. The County 2019 record proves an 845 sq ft addition was proposed and variances approved, but no permit/as-built/completion evidence was found. The 2022 newsletter photo and unchanged-building remark are not conclusive completion records.

remaining_uncertainty: The County record documents an 845 sq ft addition proposal; it is uncertain whether/when it was completed. The candidate feature area aligns closely with the pre-addition 6,500 sq ft report.
The campus coordinate conversion is a local approximation, not a surveyed CRS transformation.
No measured height, roof pitch, eave depth, architectural elevations, or georeferenced facade dimensions are available; height is intentionally unverified and is a display placeholder only.
The proposed 845 sq ft 2019 addition completion remains unresolved. The model preserves GIS feature 803 / the approximately 6,500 sq ft pre-addition footprint.
The 2022 photo directly supports general facade and roof character but not compass direction, exact entry location, window count, or dimensions.

changes: Replaced dark red/charcoal scheme with photo-supported light buff masonry and pale broad flat eave.
Reworked facade as repeated taller multi-pane window bays, visible entry glazing, and a central masonry/sign-panel cue.
Kept the GIS feature 803 shell polygon unchanged and kept 3.6576 m explicitly as an unverified display placeholder.
revision_2026_10_26.addition_decision: 2019 proposed 845 sq ft addition status unresolved; retain pre-addition GIS footprint pending as-built evidence.
